cold_open.hook: Walmart stock tanked 7.4% today because the company wants to give you cheaper groceries—and Wall Street hates when retailers actually pass savings to customers.

markets.macro_note: Broad weakness across tech and retail; VIX dips to 17.35 as macro anxiety eases but earnings reality bites.

big_story.story_title: SpaceX is heavily reliant on Starlink for growth and profit as it marches toward Nasdaq listing
big_story.angle: SpaceX's IPO filing reveals Starlink is the profit engine, not rockets—and that's either a genius diversification or a sign Elon's betting the farm on satellite internet instead of Mars.

quick_hits.angle: Anthropic is paying $15B/year for Elon's data centers while Elon's company is going public—this is the Crocs IPO of corporate governance, where the CEO's side hustle becomes the main character.
Air France and Airbus convicted of manslaughter in 2009 crash—15 years later, European courts finally decided 'too big to fail' doesn't mean 'too big to prosecute.'
Spotify stock pops on first investor day since 2022—the streaming wars are over, and the winner is the company that convinced Wall Street podcasts are a moat.
White House postpones AI executive order signing ceremony—nothing says 'we have a coherent AI strategy' like canceling the photo op.

odd_thing.joke_angle: A literary AI scandal that 'changes everything'—in media, 'changes everything' is what we say when we're too embarrassed to admit nothing changed.

sign_off.callback_target: Walmart's tariff refund gamble—the one company that chose to actually help shoppers instead of buying back stock.
